name: United States
description: The United States from the first colonies through revolution, civil war and two world wars to the Moon landing and the present.

checkpoints.name: The colonies
checkpoints.note: English settlers found Jamestown and Plymouth on land long home to Native nations. Thirteen colonies grow on farming, trade and the labour of enslaved Africans.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and a new nation
checkpoints.note: Taxes from London spark a revolution. The colonies declare independence in 1776, win the war, write the Constitution and elect George Washington the first president.

checkpoints.name: Westward growth and slavery
checkpoints.note: The country pushes west, driving Native nations from their land, and wins half of Mexico. The fight over slavery in the new states splits North and South.

checkpoints.name: Civil War and Reconstruction
checkpoints.note: Eleven Southern states leave the Union and war follows. Lincoln frees the enslaved and is murdered as the war ends, and Reconstruction tries to rebuild the South.

checkpoints.name: Industry and reform
checkpoints.note: Railways, steel and oil make the country the largest economy in the world. Millions of immigrants arrive, and presidents such as Theodore Roosevelt take on the big companies.

checkpoints.name: World wars and the Depression
checkpoints.note: The United States joins World War I, then booms and falls into the Great Depression. Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal fights it, and the country leads the Allies to victory in World War II.

checkpoints.name: Superpower
checkpoints.note: The United States leads the West in the Cold War, lands on the Moon and ends segregation. It fights in Korea and Vietnam, and Watergate brings down a president.

checkpoints.name: The new century
checkpoints.note: After the Cold War the country leads the internet age. The attacks of 2001 lead to long wars, Barack Obama becomes the first Black president, and Donald Trump wins two terms.
